mesan: Movement for the Social Evolution of Black Africa: Political party in the Central African Republic.
mescal: A Mexican alcoholic drink distilled from the fermented juice of the agave.
mescaline: A hallucinogenic and intoxicating compound present in the peyote cactus (Lophophora williamsii), the San Pedro cactus (Echinopsis pachanoi), and the Peruvian torch (Echinopsis peruviana).
meself: Me, as direct or indirect object the speaker as the object of a verb or preposition, when the speaker is also the subject.
mesembryanthemum: Genus of succulent plants indigenous to southern Africa.
mesenchymal: Of or pertaining to the mesenchyme.
mesenchymal cell: A type of multipotent stromal cell that differentiates into many other types of cells, chondrocytes, osteoblasts, and adipocytes.
mesenchymal tissue: That part of the mesoderm of an embryo that develops into connective tissue, bone, cartilage, etc
mesenchyme: That part of the mesoderm of an embryo that develops into connective tissue, bone, cartilage, etc
mesenteric artery: One of the vessels which supplies blood from the aorta and distribute it to a large portion of the gastrointestinal tract.
mesh network: A communications network with at least two pathways to each node, forming a net-like organization. When each node is connected to every other node, the network is said to be fully meshed. When only some of the nodes are linked, switching is required to make all the connections and the network is said to be partially meshed, or partially connected.
meshwork: A net; an assembly of meshes.
mesial: Pertaining to the midline of the body.
Facing the side of a tooth which faces the middle of the jaw.
mesic: Characterized by an intermediate degree of moisture, in between xeric (dry) and hydric (wet); somewhat moist.
Adapted to a habitat of intermediate moisture.
Of or pertaining to mesons; mesonic.
mesmeric: Of or relating to mesmerism or mesmerization.
mesmerise: To exercise mesmerism on; to affect another person, such as to heal or soothe, through the use of animal magnetism.
mesmerism: The method or power of gaining control over someone's personality or actions.
The theory and practice of Mesmer himself or his disciples, which involved hypnosis and a superstructure of theory that included animal magnetism.
The state induced by hypnotic methods (especially those of Mesmer himself).
meso: In between the "macro" and "micro" levels of sociological structures.
Of a tactic diad, having structural units in identical orientation.
mesoamerica: Historical region and cultural area in southern North America and most of Central America.
A pre-Columbian cultural region extending from southern Mexico to roughly the area that comprises modern Honduras and El Salvador.
mesocratic: Relating to mesocracy, or rule by the middle class.
Neither leucocratic nor melanocratic; having a more or less even mixture of light and dark constituents.
The second stage of interglacial forest development (Early-Temperate), characterized by a transitional mix of light-demanding and shade-tolerant species.
mesoderm: One of the three tissue layers in the embryo of a metazoan animal, which will produce, through development, many internal organs of the adult, e.g. muscles, spine and the circulatory system.
mesolithic: Of or referring to the Middle Stone Age (also the Mesolithic period or the Mesolithic age), a prehistoric period that lasted between 10000 and 3000 BC.
meson: The mesial plane dividing the body into similar right and left halves.
An elementary particle that is composed of a quark and an antiquark, such as a kaon or pion. (Mesons composed of rarer quarks are much heavier.)
mesonephros: The second of the three excretory organs of the developing embryo; the Wolffian body.
mesopelagic: Describing the pelagic zone of the ocean between the photic epipelagic and the aphotic bathypelagic zones, characterized by very minimal light.
mesopelagic zone: The part of the ocean where there is very minimal light, located below the photic epipelagic zone but above the aphotic bathypelagic zone.
mesophyll: The soft internal parenchyma of a leaf.
A leaf of middling size, between macrophyll and microphyll.
mesopleuron: The lateral surface of the mesothorax
mesospheric: Of or pertaining to the mesosphere.
mesquite: Any of several deciduous trees of the genus Prosopis found in America, and used as forage, which have long, beige seed and bean pods which may be dried and ground into a sweet, nutty flour.
The wood of these trees, used for smoking food, or charcoal made from this wood.
Country or land dominated by mesquite trees.
mesquite grass: Certain pasture grasses commonly found growing alongside mesquite trees, specifically Bouteloua oligostachya.
mess about: To be in a casual non-committal relationship
To play with; to toy with; to waste the time of (a person).
mess around: To have a sexual relationship, especially one which is noncommittal.
mess hall: A military dining room or building on an army or marine base.
mess kit: A compact set of eating utensils (including plate, cup, utensils) and sometimes cooking pots etc, used in the field by soldiers and by campers.
A small bag used to carry one's personal effects or toiletries while traveling.
A formal uniform, worn for occasions such as mess dinners.
mess of pottage: Something of trivial value, especially of immediate value.
mess over: To mistreat, abuse, oppress or bother (someone).
mess tin: A portable container for cooking or serving food, originally for military use, and generally of a rounded rectangular form.
mess up: To make a mess of; to untidy, disorder, soil, or muss.
To cause a problem with; to introduce an error or mistake in; to make muddled or confused; spoil; ruin.
To botch, bungle; to perform poorly on.
To make a mistake; to do something incorrectly; to perform poorly.
mess with: To joke around with or dupe someone, in either a friendly or unfriendly manner.
To admire, enjoy, or approve of.
mess with the bull and you get the horns: Synonym of when you mess with the bull, you get the horns.
message board: A board on which messages may be posted, especially one in a public space.
A system by which users may send, read and reply to public messages; an electronic bulletin board or forum.
message control: The management of an organization’s communicating its own agenda to the public, particularly as shaped by news media, customers or others.
message fiction: Fiction that attempts to convey a sociopolitical message, as opposed to mere escapism.
message in a bottle: A message written on a scrap of paper, rolled up and put in an empty bottle and set adrift on the ocean; traditionally, a method used by castaways to advertise their distress to the outside world.

An analogous message sent off into the world or universe without knowledge of who the recipient will be: plaques on craft launched into outer space, interstellar radio messages, stationary time capsules, balloon mail, and so on.
message queue: A queue onto which messages may be placed for delivery between components as part of interprocess communication.
message unit: An individual broadcasting slot, such as a single televised advertisement.
messed up: Morally reprehensible; clearly and grossly objectionable.
messenger bag: A sack worn over one shoulder with a strap winding around the chest, traditionally used by bicycle messengers.
messenger rna: RNA that encodes and carries information from DNA during transcription to sites of protein synthesis to undergo translation in order to yield a protein.
messenia: A regional unit in the south-western Peloponnese, Greece, which has its modern capital at Kalamata. The original capital was at Messene.
messianic: Of, relating to, or resembling a messiah or the Messiah.
Of, relating to, or resembling messianism.
messidor: Tenth month of the French Republican Calendar.
The tenth month of the French Republican Calendar, from June 19 or 20 to July 18 or 19.
messily: In a messy manner; sloppily, shoddily.
messinian: Sixth and last age of the Miocene epoch.
The final subdivision of the Miocene epoch.
messinian salinity crisis: A geological event, characterized by the partial desiccation of the Mediterranean basin.
messmate: An associate with whom one shares a mess (eating place) on a ship.
Any of various eucalypts with rough bark, specifically Eucalyptus obliqua.
messuage: Originally, a plot of land as the site for a dwelling house and its appurtenant interests; now, a dwelling house or residential building together with its outbuildings and assigned land.
mestizo: A person of mixed ancestry, especially one of Spanish and Native American heritage.

A person of mixed ancestry, especially one of Austronesian Filipino and Spanish or Chinese ancestry, such as that of the Spanish mestizos and Chinese mestizos from the Spanish Colonial Era of the Philippines.
metre: The basic unit of length in the International System of Units (SI: Système International d'Unités), equal to the distance travelled by light in a vacuum in 1/299 792 458 seconds. The metre is equal to 39+⁴⁷⁄₁₂₇ (approximately 39.37) imperial inches.
meta: metamour: In a polyamorous relationship, one's partner's partner, with whom one is not directly involved.
Self-referential; structured analogously (structured by relationships), but at a higher level.
meta tag: Text inserted into the source code of a web page to provide metadata, such as keywords for a search engine.
